audit_findings.title: The earnings anchor still includes a business stream that has effectively disappeared
audit_findings.magnitude: FY2025 USAID revenue $576.4 million; 9M FY2026 USAID/DOS revenue declined by $360 million, from approximately $550 million to $190 million; owner-earnings effect unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: The historical-trend anchor and forecast growth capitalize earnings from the former USAID perimeter without a continuing-business adjustment.
audit_findings.evidence: We currently expect no significant USAID revenue in fiscal 2026.
audit_findings.explanation: The revenue contraction and historical-perimeter mismatch are demonstrated, although complete disappearance and the resulting owner-earnings loss are not: cost reductions, working-capital releases, acquisitions and replacement work may offset part of it. A stream equal to 10.6% of FY2025 revenue is large enough to make the $416 million anchor and scenario values materially unreliable until reconciled.
audit_findings.action: Reconstruct trailing and forward owner earnings excluding terminated USAID work, separately identifying retained DOS work, stranded costs, termination collections, working-capital releases, replacement-contract margins and acquired earnings; rerun every scenario from that continuing-business anchor.

audit_findings.title: Historical growth may require acquisition spending excluded from owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: RPS purchase price $784 million; acquisition cash outlays $97.263 million in FY2025 and $191.870 million in 9M FY2026
audit_findings.mechanism: Acquired earnings increase the historical OE trend and forecast growth, while acquisition consideration is excluded from operating owner earnings and the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: We view acquisitions as a key component in the execution of our growth strategy, and we intend to use cash, debt or equity, as we deem appropriate, to fund acquisitions.
audit_findings.explanation: The acquisition dependence and excluded cash outlays are demonstrated, but the portion of the forecast 8%-10% growth that requires acquisitions remains unresolved. RPS alone cost about 10.2% of the $7.694 billion base operating value, and continued acquisitions remain an explicit strategy, so treating acquisition-assisted growth as costless could materially overstate distributable value.
audit_findings.action: Decompose historical OE growth into organic, acquired and divested components; support forecast growth with organic evidence or deduct acquisition consideration, integration costs and associated financing needed to produce each scenario's growth, then rerun the valuation.

audit_findings.title: Contingent acquisition consideration is a claim ahead of common equity missing from the bridge
audit_findings.magnitude: Latest recorded contingent consideration $113.783 million, or $0.42 per diluted share and 1.44% of base equity value; maximum potential outstanding $215.441 million, or $0.79 per share and 2.72% of base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: An unpaid acquisition-financing obligation is absent from the common-equity bridge while related fair-value adjustments may have been normalized out of OE.
audit_findings.evidence: This amount consisted of $ 104 million in initial cash payments and $ 43 million of the estimated fair value of contingent earn-out obligations, with a maximum of $ 60 million, based on the achievement of specified operating income targets in each of the three years following their respective acquisition dates.
audit_findings.explanation: The latest balance sheet demonstrates a $113.783 million liability. Even deducting the filed maximum potential amount would reduce base value from $28.91 to about $28.12 per share and bull value from $32.15 to about $31.36, both still below the $35.91 market price. It therefore does not change the current valuation conclusion, although the bridge should be corrected.
audit_findings.action: Confirm the portion of the $113.783 million balance comprising earn-outs versus escrow holdbacks, trace all remeasurement adjustments and payments through normalized OE, and deduct the otherwise-unrecognized obligation in a bridge rerun.

audit_findings.title: Normalization may have removed an unresolved legal claim without reserving it in equity value
audit_findings.magnitude: Filed ancillary-claim estimate $18.0 million, equal to $0.07 per diluted share and 0.23% of base equity value; excess uninsured exposure unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: If the legal charge was added back to OE while an unpaid reserve or additional uninsured exposure was not deducted in the bridge, the same claim is omitted from both components.
audit_findings.evidence: The settlement agreement and consent decree do not resolve these ancillary claims.
audit_findings.explanation: The ongoing ancillary claims and original $18 million estimate are demonstrated, but the record does not establish whether that amount remains accrued, was included in the OE normalization, or adequately covers final exposure. The filed estimate alone is not material relative to $7.925 billion of base equity value, but the unresolved excess and insurance collectibility cannot be scaled from the supplied record.
audit_findings.action: Trace the $18 million reserve through the latest liability ledger and cash payments, identify the exact legal amount added back in each OE year, obtain current claim ranges and coverage positions, exclude unrecognized insurance recoveries, and rerun OE or the bridge for any uncovered amount.

audit_findings.title: The cash addition may include operating cash rather than distributable excess cash
audit_findings.magnitude: Maximum disputed addition $230.835 million, or $0.84 per diluted share and 2.91% of base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: The bridge adds all cash after removing interest income, potentially double-counting cash required to support the capitalized operating business or satisfy existing obligations.
audit_findings.evidence: Our primary uses of cash are to fund working capital, cash dividends, share repurchases, capital expenditures and repayment of debt, as well as to fund acquisitions and earn-out obligations from prior acquisitions.
audit_findings.explanation: The valuation demonstrably adds the entire $230.835 million balance, but the required operating portion is unresolved. Even the conservative removal of all cash would reduce base value to about $28.07 and bull value to about $31.31 per share, still below the $35.91 price; the base-derived buy-below level would fall only from $20.24 to about $19.65. The issue therefore cannot change the current conclusion at its maximum filed scale.
audit_findings.action: Classify restricted, foreign, project-support and minimum operating cash; reserve cash for earn-outs, litigation, taxes and seasonal working capital; then rerun the bridge using only evidenced excess cash.

audit_findings.title: Unconsolidated venture guarantees can create unrecorded claims ahead of shareholders
audit_findings.mechanism: Uncovered guarantee payments would reduce OE when incurred or require a bridge deduction for a present claim ahead of common equity.
audit_findings.evidence: In the ordinary course of business, we enter into various agreements as part of certain unconsolidated subsidiaries, joint ventures and other jointly executed contracts where we are jointly and severally liable.
audit_findings.explanation: Joint-and-several obligations are demonstrated, but no probable loss, maximum exposure or uncovered net amount is supplied. The filing states that total potential payments cannot be estimated and notes possible client or third-party recovery, so the record cannot establish materiality or a valuation adjustment.
audit_findings.action: Obtain contract-level guarantee, surety and joint-venture schedules; identify remaining completion costs, billable amounts, troubled projects, collateral, recourse, insurance and existing accruals; probability-weight any uncovered exposure and rerun the bridge if material.
